text:
Detroit and Colorado both arrive on the back of one-goal losses two nights ago. The Red Wings fell 2-1 to Vegas when Trevor Connelly scored with 1:42 left, and they're 2-3-0 in their last five. They're also without Dylan Larkin, who is serving a suspension and has an estimated return of Nov 14. In the five games since he went out, Alex DeBrincat has taken his spot beside Lucas Raymond and Arvidsson, and Emmitt Finnie has moved onto the first power-play unit. Colorado lost 3-2 in overtime to Nashville, on a night Vitali Pinchuk scored his first NHL goal, and sits 3-1-1 over its last five without Josh Manson.

The chance numbers are close. At five on five, both teams have taken 53% of the expected goals (the quality of shots each side creates and allows). Colorado has the edge in chance creation, 3.40 expected goals per 60 minutes to Detroit's 3.24, and on the penalty kill. Our model has Colorado at 3.20 goals tonight and Detroit at 2.87. In net, projected starter Daniil Tarasov is at +7.2 goals saved above expected this season but was -2.8 last year, while Mackenzie Blackwood is at -0.5 after a +8.0 season.

Nathan MacKinnon is our top Colorado pick, with a 39% chance to score and an 84% chance to record a point, and Artturi Lehkonen has 11 points in his last ten. For Detroit, Arvidsson plays his 700th game, and Prashanth Iyer of Expected By Whom posted that in Finnie "the Wings have finally found" their 1C, with a note of "slightest of hyperbole."
